entries.name: JoAnna Mendoza
entries.headline: Proud mom, dedicated public servant, & retired U.S. Marine.
entries.summary: JoAnna has spent her life answering the call to serve, from defending the nation and training future military leaders to helping veterans navigate broken systems. Now she is running to represent Arizona's 6th Congressional District, bringing battle-tested leadership to Washington to fight for working families and lower the costs of food, gas, housing, and child care.

entries.name: Katie Hobbs
entries.headline: Protecting democracy in Arizona
entries.summary: Governor Katie Hobbs has protected all Arizonans from a corrupt and abusive federal government. During her time in office, Katie has granted tax rebates to Arizonan families, defended reporductive rights, and passed policy to protect our water. She is running for again to continue making a positive impact on the lives of of Arizonans.

entries.name: Dr. Amelia Gallitano-Mendel
entries.headline: Tenured professor dedicated to innovative solutions
entries.summary: Dr. Gallitano is running to represent Arizona's 2nd Legislative District in the Senate. She runs as an advocate for Arizonan families and and seeks to lower the costs of every day life. She is commited to practical, evidence based solutions that will protect our future and bring integrity to the State Senate.
entries.photo_credit: Arizona List / WomenCount, used with permission

entries.name: Kiana Maria Sears
entries.headline: Continuing more than 20 years of public service
entries.summary: As an Arizona State Senator, Kiana has been a champion for Arizonan families. She has funded nutrition programs, fought for affordable housing, and protected public education. Kiana is running to represent Arizona's 9th Legislative District in the Senate in order to continue her service.
why_bullets: Access to healthcare and nutritious meals
Access to community centered, obtainable affordable housing
entries.photo_credit: Arizona List / WomenCount, used with permission

entries.name: Kristie O'Brien
entries.headline: Lawyer-turned-mediator committed to Arizona
entries.summary: Kristie has centered her life around public service. After spending time working on Capitol Hill to craft policy and staff 10 senators, she came home to Arizona and serve as a lawyer to protect people's rights. Now, she is running to represent Arizona's 13th Legislative District in the Senate so that she can work to bring common-sense solutions to the table.
entries.photo_credit: Arizona List / WomenCount, used with permission

entries.name: Elaine Aldrete
entries.headline: Experienced community leader devoted to Arizona
entries.summary: Elaine has undertaken numerous projects in her community to further the lives of those around her, including starting her non-profit Teaching Life Choices and serving as a State Committee Member. She is now running for Arizona's 16th Legislative District in the Senate to pursue advocating for affordable healthcare, housing, and utilities.
entries.photo_credit: Arizona List / WomenCount, used with permission

entries.name: Rep. Nancy Gutierrez
entries.headline: A teacher's voice for Arizona!
entries.summary: Nancy serves as the Assistant Minority Leader in the AZ State House. She's the Ranking member on the Education Committee and is on the Appropriations Committee. She attended public school in Arizona from K-12 to earning a Bachelor of Science in Elementary Education with an emphasis in Mathematics.

entries.name: Stephanie Simacek
entries.headline: Mother and representative proud to advocate for all
entries.summary: Stephanie is passionate about public education and has advocated as a state representative for tighter control Arizona's ESA program to ensure that our schools can be properly funded. Likewise, Stephanie also recognizes the lack of basic affordability impacting Arizonans and seeks to hold corporate companies accountable. To continue her service, she is running for Arizona's 2nd Legislative District in the House.
entries.photo_credit: Arizona List / WomenCount, used with permission

entries.name: Karen Gresham
entries.headline: Third generation Arizonan committed to public service
entries.summary: Karen has a background in budgeting and analyzinag data as well as in public education advocacy. She has served on Madison Elementary School District's governing board and now seeks to advocate for the needs of teachers, parents, and students on a higher policy level by running for the State House as a representative of Legislative District 4.
entries.photo_credit: Arizona List / WomenCount, used with permission

entries.name: Tammy Caputi
entries.headline: Experienced community leader focused on practical results
entries.summary: Caputi's campaign emphasizes practical leadership, integrity, and community-focused problem solving. Her priorities are centered on safer communities, economic opportunity, and responsible government. She is running for Arizona's 4th Legislative District in the house.
entries.photo_credit: Arizona List / WomenCount, used with permission

entries.name: Lorena Austin
entries.headline: Fifth-generation Arizonan and community-rooted legislator
entries.summary: Austin's campaign highlights deep Mesa roots and a record of community advocacy. Her focus is on strengthening public education, addressing housing costs, and protecting Arizona's long-term water future. She is running for Arizona's 9th Legislative District in the House.
entries.photo_credit: Arizona List / WomenCount, used with permission

entries.name: Rockee Armstrong
entries.headline: Educator, administrator, and advocate for stronger schools
entries.summary: Dr. Racquel 'Rockee' Armstrong brings experience as a teacher, school administrator, and advocate for education. She is running to represent Arizona's 13th Legislative District in the House and is campaigning on stronger schools, affordable housing, and a more secure future for Arizona families.
entries.photo_credit: Arizona List / WomenCount, used with permission

entries.name: Julia Gusse
entries.headline: Air Force veteran and former Maricopa councilmember
entries.summary: Gusse has previously served in the Air Force and has local-government experience. Now, she seeks to continue her service by running in Arizona's 16th Legislative District in the House. She is committed to practical, people-first leadership focused on veterans, schools, public safety, and reducing household costs.
entries.photo_credit: Arizona List / WomenCount, used with permission

entries.name: Holly Lyon
entries.headline: Retired Air Force colonel, educator, and civic leader
entries.summary: Holly served 26 years in the Air Force and forged consensus on intense negotiations to save $100 million. Additionally, she has also served as an educator, technology consultant, and civic leader. Holly now runs to conitnue her service as a representative in Arizona's 17th Legislative District.
entries.photo_credit: Arizona List / WomenCount, used with permission

entries.name: Deborah Howard
entries.headline: Public-affairs professional and longtime civic advocate
entries.summary: Deborah's background includes experience with both non-profit and private-sector public affairs. She has a passion for issues such as affordable living, healthcare, public education, and voting rights. Deborah has centered her campaign on accountable democracy and is running to represent Arizona's 27th Legislative District in the House.
entries.photo_credit: Arizona List / WomenCount, used with permission

entries.name: Amish Shah
entries.headline: Emergency physician and former Arizona state legislator
entries.summary: Dr. Amish Shah is a board-certified emergency physician and former state representative.  His public-service record centers on healthcare, education, working families, and pragmatic lawmaking, and he is now running to represent Arizona's 1st Congressional District.

entries.name: Jonathan Nez
entries.headline: Former Navajo Nation president and rural Arizona leader
entries.summary: Nez grew up in northern Arizona without basic utilities and later served as Navajo Nation president, shaping a campaign focused on rural infrastructure, water, jobs, energy costs, and bipartisan problem solving.

entries.name: Yassamin Ansari
entries.headline: Congresswoman and former Phoenix vice mayor
entries.summary: Yassamin's public-service background includes both local and federal leadership, where she worked on climate action, transportation, homelessness, and affordable housing. She is now running to continue her representation of Arizona's 3rd Congressional District.

entries.name: Greg Stanton
entries.headline: Former Phoenix mayor and experienced congressional lawmaker
entries.summary: Greg's experience comes from serving previoulsy the mayor of Phoenix and as a member of Congress. His priorities include practical results on infrastructure, household costs, education, economic growth, and public safety. Greg is eager to continue serving the State of Arizona and is running to represent Arizona's 4th Congressional District.

entries.name: Elizabeth Lee
entries.headline: Registered nurse and working-family advocate
entries.summary: Elizabeth's experience and passions come from her background as a nurse and mother. She emphasizes affordability, reproductive healthcare, and accountability. Drawing on her background in healthcare, Elizabeth is running to represent Arizona's 5th Congressional District.

entries.name: Adelita Grijalva
entries.headline: Longtime Southern Arizona public servant and community leader
entries.summary: Adelita draws from her deep Southern Arizona roots and years of public service as she runs to continue her representation of Arizona's 7th Congressional Distric. Her focus is on bringing people together, protecting communities, and expanding opportunity for families.
entries.photo_credit: Damien Salas, Office of the Clerk U.S.House of Representatives

entries.name: Bernadette Greene-Placentia
entries.headline: Trucker, small-business owner, and working-class advocate
entries.summary: Bernadette is a mother, long-haul trucker, and small-business owner who has logged more than four million miles. Now, she is drawinging from firsthand experience as she runs to represent Arizona's 8th Congressional District. She is passionate about affordability, immigration, and veterans.

entries.name: Danielle Sterbinsky
entries.headline: Navy veteran, working mother, and operations specialist
entries.summary: Dani's experience comes from serving  in the U.S. Navy aboard the USS Bainbridge and later building a career in operations. She is passionate about housing, education, and rural & community investment. Dani runs as a veteran, working mom, and Arizonan neighbor to represent Arizona's 9th Congressional District.

entries.name: Adrian Fontes
entries.headline: Marine veteran, attorney, and Arizona Secretary of State
entries.summary: Adrian is an Arizona native, Marine veteran, former prosecutor, and now serves as Arizona's current Sectretary of State. His work has focused on voter access, ballot security and transparency, and he is running to continue his service as Secretary of State.

entries.name: Kris Mayes
entries.headline: Attorney General and longtime consumer advocate
entries.summary: Mayes grew up in Prescott and has served as a statewide utility regulator, professor, and Arizona Attorney General. She has a record of fiercely fighting for Arizona and seeks to continue her advocacy by running to maintain her position of Attorney General.

entries.name: Nick Mansour
entries.headline: Entrepreneur and education leader running as a fiscal watchdog
entries.summary: Nick is an Arizona-raised father and entrepreneur who built a nursing school. He has a passion for eliminating waste, fraud, and government abuse. Drawing from his experiences, he now runs for the position of Arizona State Treasurer.

entries.name: Teresa Leyba Ruiz
entries.headline: Veteran educator and former community-college president
entries.summary: Terry is a native Arizonan and first-generation college graduate. She brings with her 35 years of experience in education as a math teacher, administrator, and community-college president, and now she is running for Superintedent of Public Instruction to further her service of Arizona.

entries.name: Brian Matlock
entries.headline: Marine veteran, engineer, and mining-safety professional
entries.summary: Brian is a Marine Reserve veteran and mechanical engineer. He has earned decades of experience in mining and heavy industry, and he is dedicated to mine safety, protecting workers, and technical interprise. Drawing from his experience, he now seeks to serve Arizona's mines and mine workers by running for State Mine Inspector.

entries.name: Jonathon Hill
entries.headline: Consumer-focused utility and energy-policy advocate
entries.summary: Dr. Jonathon's experience comes from his background as a scientist and engineer. To help restore transparency and accountability of the Arizona Corporate Commision, he is running for a seat as Commissioner. His priorities are lowering utility bills, protecting Arizona's water, scrutinizing large data-center demands.

entries.name: Clara Pratte
entries.headline: Navajo entrepreneur and rural-infrastructure leader
entries.summary: Clara is a Navajo Nation member and has advised U.S. and Navajo leaders. Having grown up without access to utilities, she understands and respects the need them. Taking this passion, Clara co-founded an energy company focused on infrastructure and economic opportunity in underserved communities, and she now for for Commissioner on Arizona Corporate Commission.

entries.name: Christine Dargon
entries.headline: Educator, social-service professional, and rural community advocate
entries.summary: Dr. Christine has more than 30 years in education and social service. Now, she is running to represent Arizona's 1st Legislative District in the Senate.She is passionate about the needs of rural communities and prioritizes funding for education, water supply and quality, and common sense gun laws.

entries.name: Jeff Fortney
entries.headline: Special-education teacher and school-board leader
entries.summary: Jeff left a long career in computer programming to become a special-education teacher and has served on the Cave Creek Unified School District governing board since 2020. His experience as a teacher and board member has fostered his passions for public education, affordability, and people's rights. Now, he is running to represent Arizona's 3rd Legislative District in the Senate.

entries.name: Aaron Lieberman
entries.headline: Arizona entrepreneur, education innovator, and former legislator
entries.summary: Aaron is an Arizona native and Yale graduate. Taking his experience and resources, he founded two national early-childhood organizations that created thousands of jobs and served more than one million children. He is now running to represent Arizona's 4th Legislative in the Senate and seeks to work across the aisle to improve the lives of Arizonans.

entries.name: Christine Marsh
entries.headline: Arizona Teacher of the Year and veteran public-school educator
entries.summary: Christine spent more than three decades in Arizona classrooms and was named the 2016 Arizona Teacher of the Year, and she has served previously in the Arizona Senate. Her experiences both professionally and personally have fostered a passion for public education, Arizona's economy, and addressing the opiod crisis. Christine now runs to represent Arizona's 5th Legislative District again in the Senate.

entries.name: Blair Moses
entries.headline: Retired attorney with healthcare and legislative-analysis experience
entries.summary: Blair's experience comes from being a retired attorney with a prior healthcare career. Having this intersection of perspectives, she is running to represent Arizona's 10th Legislative District in the Senate. Her priorities include constitutional rights, healthcare access, and protections for vulnerable communities.

entries.name: Catherine Miranda
entries.headline: Educator and experienced legislator with deep district roots
entries.summary: Catherine is native to District 11 and has a background in education as well as having served in both chambers of the Arizona Legislature. As Senator, Catherine has ben dedicated to the values of her community and is running to continue her representation of Arizona's 11th Legislative District in the Senate.

entries.name: Patty Contreras
entries.headline: Retired Phoenix public servant and experienced state representative
entries.summary: Patty served for more than 31 years with the City of Phoenix, where she worked in providing programs and resources for seniors. Given her background as both an Arizonan native and in public policy, Patty is committed to Arizona's environment, seniors, and veterans. She now runs to represent Arizona's 12th Legislative District in the Senate.

entries.name: Stephanie Walsh
entries.headline: Engineer and business leader focused on practical solutions
entries.summary: Stephanie is a mechanical engineer, business owner, and nonprofit leader. Her experience has fueled a passion for reliable energy, responsible water management, public education, and a robust economy. She is running to represent Arizona's 14th Legistive District in the Senate.

entries.name: Edgar Soto
entries.headline: Marine veteran, lifelong educator, and community leader
entries.summary: Soto has more than 30 years in education from K-12 through higher education and brings experience as a Marine veteran, educator, coach, and community leader.

entries.name: Priya Sundareshan
entries.headline: Natural-resources attorney, educator, and State Senate leader
entries.summary: Sundareshan was born and raised in Tucson, studied engineering at MIT and law and natural-resource economics at the University of Arizona, and has worked on natural resources and voting rights.

entries.name: Ryan Slawson
entries.headline: Army veteran, software developer, and small-business owner
entries.summary: Slawson served nine years as an Army intelligence collector with two Iraq deployments, has worked as a software developer for more than a decade, and has nearly 15 years of small-business experience.

entries.name: Rosanna Gabaldón
entries.headline: Experienced Southern Arizona legislator and local-government leader
entries.summary: Gabald├│n has served Southern Arizona as a town councilmember, state representative, and state senator, with a record emphasizing collaboration, public education, economic development, and water sustainability.

entries.name: Eva Diaz
entries.headline: Lifelong educator and experienced Arizona state senator
entries.summary: Dr. Eva Diaz has served in the Arizona Senate since 2022 and draws on a career in education to advocate for public schools, healthcare, working families, housing, and equal rights.

entries.name: Brian Fernandez
entries.headline: Yuma native, entrepreneur, and experienced state senator
entries.summary: Fernandez is a sixth-generation Arizonan who attended Yuma public schools, founded and sold a software company, and later entered public service focused on rural communities, education, water, transportation, and jobs.

entries.name: Analise Ortiz
entries.headline: Former investigative journalist and civil-rights advocate
entries.summary: Ortiz is an Arizona native and former investigative journalist whose public-service work includes civil-rights advocacy and legislative action on worker safety, childcare, homelessness, roads, and government accountability.

entries.name: Laura Huber
entries.headline: Licensed counselor and fifth-generation farm-family advocate
entries.summary: Huber is a licensed professional counselor from five generations of farmers and ranchers, with frontline mental-health experience in crisis response, psychiatric care, corrections, and homelessness outreach.

entries.name: Flavio Bravo
entries.headline: Fifth-generation Arizonan and experienced state senator
entries.summary: Bravo was born and raised in District 26, is a first-generation college graduate, and has combined legislative service with nonprofit and community leadership focused on housing, education, jobs, and healthcare.

entries.name: Kyle Clayton
entries.headline: School-board president and data-driven community advocate
entries.summary: Clayton is a lifelong District 27 resident, Realtor, and Washington Elementary School District governing-board president who emphasizes analytical decision-making, transparency, and student- and family-focused leadership.

entries.name: Michael Braun
entries.headline: Community-focused candidate emphasizing service and collaboration
entries.summary: Braun's campaign stresses listening, problem solving, and active constituent service, with priorities spanning water, the economy, energy, education funding, rights, veterans, taxes, and the state budget.

entries.name: Eric Stafford
entries.headline: Lifelong Arizonan, tradesman, organizer, and small-business advocate
entries.summary: Stafford is an Arizona native with experience as an airframe-and-powerplant mechanic, machinist, veterinary technician, political organizer, and small-business advocate.

entries.name: Lauren Kuby
entries.headline: State senator, former Tempe vice mayor, and sustainability scientist
entries.summary: Kuby is a former Tempe councilmember and vice mayor and an ASU sustainability scientist with a long record on environmental, consumer, worker, housing, and voting-rights issues.

entries.name: Alma Hernandez
entries.headline: Public-health professional and experienced Tucson legislator
entries.summary: Hernandez was born and raised on Tucson's south side, attended local public schools, and trained in public health, bringing that background to legislative work on healthcare, affordability, housing, and family economic security.

entries.name: Mae Peshlakai
entries.headline: Veteran public servant representing rural and tribal Arizona
entries.summary: Peshlakai brings experience in the Arizona House and Senate, Native American liaison work, education programs, small business, and military service, with a focus on the distinctive needs of rural and tribal communities.

entries.name: Ian Teller
entries.headline: Ian is a Diné community advocate and next-generation rural leader
entries.summary: Ian Teller is a Diné leader from Tsaile, Arizona with a background in community advocacy and youth engagement.

entries.name: Janeen Connolly
entries.headline: Community-engagement professional and experienced state representative
entries.summary: Connolly spent decades building community and government relationships across Arizona, earned a master's in advocacy communication, and has brought that bridge-building background to the Legislature.

entries.name: Brian Garcia
entries.headline: Attorney, community advocate, and public-school leader
entries.summary: Garcia is an Arizona-raised attorney and first-generation graduate whose public-service background includes school-board leadership, congressional work, Tribal representation, and advocacy for unaccompanied children.

entries.name: Sally Ann Gonzales
entries.headline: Educator, Pascua Yaqui leader, and veteran Arizona lawmaker
entries.summary: Gonzales is a former elementary teacher and Pascua Yaqui Tribal Council member who became the first Indigenous woman elected to the Arizona House and has spent years advocating for children, elders, veterans, and vulnerable families.

entries.name: Betty Villegas
entries.headline: Housing expert and longtime Tucson public servant
entries.summary: Villegas is a third-generation Tucsonan with decades of public service in affordable housing and community development, including leadership roles with Pima County, South Tucson, and the Arizona Legislature.

entries.name: Sandy Zalecki
entries.headline: Veteran, small-business owner, and real-estate professional
entries.summary: Zalecki's background includes military service, ranch ownership, healthcare administration, and real estate, giving her firsthand experience with rural communities, property, and household economic concerns.

entries.name: Julie Gable
entries.headline: Business executive focused on practical, community-first solutions
entries.summary: Gable is an executive and entrepreneur whose campaign highlights experience leading organizations and a practical approach to healthcare access, technology, water security, and public education.

entries.name: Rick Spargo
entries.headline: Longtime small-business owner and civic volunteer
entries.summary: Spargo is a District 3 resident, business owner, and father of four. He has served in civic and veterans-support organizations. As State Representative, Spargo will emphasize moderation and practical problem solving.

entries.name: Sarah Liguori
entries.headline: Businesswoman, financial professional, and experienced legislator
entries.summary: Sarah is an Arizona native, mother and businesswoman. She has five years of experience as a legislator in Arizona's House of Representatives. As a representative, Sarah has fought for affordability, public education, and voting rights.

entries.name: Aaron Márquez
entries.headline: Army veteran, school-board leader, and public-service advocate
entries.summary: Aaron has served Americans both abroad and at home, ranging from two combat tours in Afghanistan, to five years on the Phoenix Union High School District governing board. As State House Representative, Aaron would fight to protect Arizona's shrinking middle class.

entries.name: Samuel Martin
entries.headline: Customer-service professional focused on constituent problem solving
entries.summary: Sam's 20+ years of experience in public-facing and technical roles has made him an expert communicator and negotiator. Sam hopes to bring his skills to the AZ House, to fight for healthcare, consumers, and education.

entries.name: Jacob Martinez
entries.headline: Mesa native, Navy reservist, and community advocate
entries.summary: Jacob is a lifelong Mesa resident, Navy reservist, and community advocate. As a state representative, Jacob will work to improve affordability, schools, and water.

entries.name: Helen Hunter
entries.headline: Chaplain, community organizer, and social-justice advocate
entries.summary: Dr. Helen Hunter is a board-certified chaplain, ordained minister and businesswoman with deep connections to both her community and faith. She is a longtime Mesa community organizer who has worked on housing, community safety, and interfaith initiatives.

entries.name: Brian Calaway
entries.headline: Former science educator and community-program leader
entries.summary: Brian left classroom teaching to build after-school enrichment programs and is now running for the AZ House. As a state legislator, Brian would advocate for access to healthcare, housing, and education.

entries.name: Oscar De Los Santos
entries.headline: House Democratic leader and former teacher
entries.summary: Oscar represents District 11 and serves as House Democratic Leader, with a legislative record that includes medical-debt relief, childcare funding, and tenant protections.

entries.name: Junelle Cavero
entries.headline: Small-business owner and longtime community advocate
entries.summary: Junelle is the daughter of hardworking immigrant parents and a small-business owner . She has spent more than 25 years in advocacy and community work, bringing family and entrepreneurial experience to the Legislature.

entries.name: Stacey Travers
entries.headline: Army veteran, geoscientist, and experienced state representative
entries.summary: Stacey Travers is a U.S. Army veteran and geoscientist. In her time at the AZ House, Stacey has advocated for veterans and emphasized bipartisan lawmaking to bring real results.

entries.name: Armando Montero
entries.headline: School-board leader with policy and public-budget experience
entries.summary: Armando joined the Tempe Union High School District board at 19 and later served as board president. As a representative, Armando will bring his six years experience to advocate for Arizonans.

entries.name: Jacob Weinberg
entries.headline: Army veteran, CPA, and technology-company finance leader
entries.summary: Jacob is a long-serving Army officer, CPA, financial auditor, and technology-company CFO. As a member of the AZ House, Jacob will bring his team-building skills to advocate for veterans, schools, and equality.

entries.name: Mary Rose
entries.headline: Third-generation Arizonan and experienced business professional
entries.summary: Mary has spent her career in large organizations and community service. As a state representative, Mary will fight for affordability, accountability, and sustainability.

entries.name: Kevin Volk
entries.headline: Small-business owner, former teacher, and bipartisan legislator
entries.summary: Kevin is a Southern Arizona native, small-business owner, and former teacher. He has been in the Arizona House of Representatives since 2025. If reelected, Kevin will use his experience to lower living costs and invest in education.

entries.name: Chris Mathis
entries.headline: Elder-law attorney, health-policy professor, and state representative
entries.summary: Mathis practices elder law and teaches health-care law and aging at the University of Arizona, bringing extensive policy experience in healthcare, long-term care, water, education, and voting rights.

entries.name: Jackie Anderson
entries.headline: Retired emergency-room nurse and rural-health advocate
entries.summary: Jackie spent more than four decades in nursing, including 19 years at an Arizona Critical Access Hospital. Her experiences have driven her to focus on healthcare access, affordability, and sustainable communities.

entries.name: Aiden Swallow
entries.headline: Army veteran focused on rural Arizona services and affordability
entries.summary: Swallow is a rural Arizona native and served nearly 20 years in Army intelligence until being abruptly removed after coming out as trans. Her experiences have not discouraged her, but rather spurred her to advocate for rural healthcare, public schools, and affordability.

entries.name: Consuelo Hernandez
entries.headline: School-board veteran and experienced state representative
entries.summary: Consuelo has served both on the Sunnyside School District governing board and in the Arizona House. She has a proven track record of voting for economic mobility, healthcare, and education.

entries.name: Miranda Lopez
entries.headline: Organizer and public-policy professional rooted in Southern Arizona
entries.summary: Miranda has worked as a campaign organizer, Pima County Democratic Party executive director, and labor leader. As LD21's representative, she will advocate for education, sustainability, and affordability.

entries.name: Elda Luna-Nájera
entries.headline: Educator, social-work professional, and community leader
entries.summary: Dr. Luna-Nájera is a native Arizonan with a doctorate in social work. Her career in social work has spurred her to run for State Representative, where she can bring opportunity to the families who need it most.

entries.name: Betsy Munoz
entries.headline: Education nonprofit leader and West Valley community advocate
entries.summary: Muñoz was born and raised in Arizona, graduated from ASU in public service and public policy. She works in educational nonprofits, helping West Valley students prepare for college and careers. Muñoz's career in education has provided insights necessary for improvements in Arizona's public school system.

entries.name: Mariana Sandoval
entries.headline: Working-family advocate and experienced state representative
entries.summary: Sandoval is a mother, community member, and legislator. Her experiences in the working class has led her to focus on affordability, jobs, and the environment.

entries.name: Emilia Cortez
entries.headline: Yuma native and bilingual public-affairs professional
entries.summary: Cortez is a Yuma native and bilingual public-affairs professional whose work spans education, nonprofits, Tribal governance, economic development, infrastructure, investment, and workforce issues.

entries.name: Alberto Flores
entries.headline: Phoenix native focused on working-family affordability
entries.summary: Flores grew up in a working-class immigrant family in Phoenix, studied political science at ASU, and is campaigning on affordability, public education, healthcare, and practical collaboration.

entries.name: Lisbeth Arescurenaga
entries.headline: Licensed mental-health professional and family advocate
entries.summary: Arescurenaga came to the United States as a teenager and built a career in social work and mental health, serving families, young people, and people facing serious health and housing challenges.

entries.name: Tiffany Byrne
entries.headline: Veteran educator and school administrator
entries.summary: Byrne has spent more than 20 years as a teacher and education leader, including K-12 science instruction and school administration, and brings firsthand experience with Arizona schools.

entries.name: Cesar Aguilar
entries.headline: Working-class Phoenix native and education-access advocate
entries.summary: Aguilar was born and raised in Phoenix, studied political science at NAU, and has led the Arizona Students' Association, organizing students and advocating for college access and affordability.

entries.name: Quantá Crews
entries.headline: State representative, property professional, and community minister
entries.summary: Crews is a property appraiser and associate minister who draws on lived experience working multiple jobs and has focused her legislative work on education, transportation, family supports, healthcare, and workforce training.

entries.name: Barbara Fike
entries.headline: Career educator running a publicly financed campaign
entries.summary: Fike is a career educator and Clean Elections candidate whose campaign focuses on schools, water management, affordable housing, reproductive healthcare, civil rights, and voting rights.

entries.name: Marc Graham
entries.headline: Air Force veteran, labor negotiator, and aviation professional
entries.summary: Graham is a retired Air Force master sergeant, former union organizer and chief negotiator, FAA-licensed aircraft technician and inspector, and aviation instructor with decades of leadership experience.

entries.name: Christine Scianna
entries.headline: Former science teacher and disability-family advocate
entries.summary: Scianna is a native Arizonan, former middle-school and science teacher, and longtime advocate for autism and disabled families who has testified at the Legislature on protections for vulnerable adults.

entries.name: Brian McMahan
entries.headline: Retired fire chief and lifelong rural public servant
entries.summary: McMahan spent roughly 40 years in public service, including as fire chief for the Parker and Buckskin Fire Districts, and emphasizes practical problem solving, transparency, rural services, and emergency-response experience.

organizations.name: Arizona Secretary of State – Elections Division
organizations.description: Arizona's chief elections office issues statewide rules for voting locations, including the 75-foot perimeter, weapons, observers, and law-enforcement presence, and operates 1-877-THE-VOTE to route reported problems to county officials or law enforcement.
ways_to_help: Report intimidation or unlawful conduct to a poll worker and 1-877-THE-VOTE
Sign up through your county to serve as a trained poll worker
Share official Arizona voting-location guidance and arizona.vote resources

organizations.name: Arizona Attorney General – Election Integrity Unit
organizations.description: The Attorney General's Office enforces certain statewide election laws, accepts first-hand civil election complaints and criminal referrals, and has litigated 2026 disputes involving federal attempts to alter Arizona election administration and mail voting.
ways_to_help: File a first-hand election complaint when conduct may violate Arizona law
Preserve specific evidence, dates, locations, and witness information
For immediate threats or crimes in progress, contact local law enforcement first

organizations.name: ACLU of Arizona
organizations.description: The ACLU of Arizona publishes 2026 voter-rights guidance, including specific information on federal agents and police at the polls, and works on election access through advocacy, education, collaboration, and litigation.
ways_to_help: Learn and share Arizona voter-rights and intimidation guidance
Report suspected civil-liberties violations or request assistance
Volunteer with the ACLU of Arizona or help monitor civil-liberties issues in your community

organizations.name: League of Women Voters of Arizona
organizations.description: The nonpartisan League engages members in Election Protection poll observation, poll-worker recruitment, voter registration, VOTE411 voter education, voting-rights advocacy, and efforts to counter election misinformation and disinformation.
ways_to_help: Volunteer as an Election Protection monitor
Help recruit or serve as a poll worker
Support voter registration, voter education, and misinformation-response work

organizations.name: Common Cause Arizona
organizations.description: Common Cause Arizona mobilizes nonpartisan Election Protection volunteers, assists voters at polling places, monitors misleading election information, promotes voter-help hotlines, and escalates major problems to election officials.
ways_to_help: Serve as a nonpartisan Election Protection volunteer
Help voters understand their rights and report intimidation or obstruction
Share 866-OUR-VOTE and Arizona voter-help resources with your community

organizations.name: Election Protection (866-OUR-VOTE)
organizations.description: Election Protection is a national, nonpartisan coalition administered by the Lawyersâ€™ Committee for Civil Rights Under Law. Trained volunteers answer voting questions, receive reports of intimidation or suppression, and provide field-based voter assistance.
ways_to_help: Volunteer for nonpartisan poll monitoring
Legal professionals can staff the Election Protection hotline
Save and share 866-OUR-VOTE and its language-access hotlines

organizations.name: Brennan Center for Justice
organizations.description: The Brennan Center's 2026 election work directly addresses armed federal agents at polling sites, voter-intimidation law, and Arizona-specific election-interference scenarios, while preparing litigation and practical guidance for voters and election officials.
ways_to_help: Use and share its 2026 safe-voting guidance
Share the Arizona Election Interference Law Handbook with election officials and community leaders
Support its legal and policy work or attend voting-rights events

organizations.name: Protect Democracy
organizations.description: Protect Democracy litigates and advocates around abuses of government power, publishes 2026 midterm guidance on federal troops and law-enforcement officers at the polls, and offers public action resources including voter-protection training and poll-worker engagement.
ways_to_help: Learn the 2026 legal limits on troops and federal agents at polling places
Use its democracy action playbook and voter-protection training resources
Sign up for updates or become a poll worker

organizations.name: Committee for Safe and Secure Elections
organizations.description: This cross-partisan group of election administrators and law-enforcement experts produces 2026 state-specific security guides, including an Arizona guide on interference and intimidation, and supports training, scenario planning, and coordinated threat response.
ways_to_help: Share the Arizona 2026 law-enforcement quick-reference guide with local officials
Encourage election officials and law enforcement to conduct scenario planning or tabletop exercises
Use its security-assessment and threat-response resources

organizations.name: Faiths United to Save Democracy (FUSD)
organizations.description: FUSD is a nonpartisan, multiracial, interfaith voter-protection campaign with Arizona as a 2026 priority state. Its Poll Chaplain/Peacekeeper program trains volunteers to provide a calm presence and de-escalate potential conflict, including scenarios involving ICE agents at polling stations.
ways_to_help: Complete 2026 Poll Chaplain/Peacekeeper training
Serve a polling-site shift in Arizona
Use 866-OUR-VOTE to report incidents and follow FUSD buddy-system and safety guidance
